original_summary: At a party, a banker and a young lawyer argue about whether death or lifelong imprisonment is more humane. The lawyer accepts a reckless bet and spends fifteen years alone in a garden lodge, reading and changing greatly while the banker loses much of his fortune. Before the deadline, the banker plans to kill the lawyer so he will not have to pay. Instead, he finds a letter saying that the lawyer rejects the money and will leave early, because his years of study have taught him to despise worldly wealth.
seed_elements: A banker and a lawyer make a reckless two-million-ruble bet about death and solitary imprisonment.
The lawyer lives alone for fifteen years in a lodge, with books and limited comforts but no human contact.
His reading moves from entertainment to serious literature, languages, philosophy, and religious writing, changing his view of life.
The banker becomes financially desperate and secretly plans to murder the lawyer before the payment is due.
The banker discovers the lawyer’s letter, which renounces the money and explains his rejection of worldly values.
The lawyer leaves voluntarily several hours before the deadline, making the banker unable to win the money and ashamed of his own plan.
discarded_elements: Detailed descriptions of the party and the lodge
Long lists of books, authors, languages, and religious or philosophical works
The banker’s extended history of bad investments
Minor watchman and household details beyond confirming that the lawyer has vanished
Excess period-specific details about Russian money and social life
conversion_plan: Keep the original historical situation rather than modernizing it, because the wager and isolation give the ending its meaning. Use third-person narration and compress the fifteen years into a few clear stages, with simple A2-level vocabulary and short sentences. Aim for about 300–350 words, preserving the bet, the lawyer’s transformation, the planned murder, the letter, and his voluntary early departure.
